Capture-recapture estimates of a hidden population

Source: R/crcap.R
crcap.Rd

How many offenders, victims or incidents no list records, from the overlap of two or three lists (police records, hospital records, a survey). With two lists the Lincoln-Petersen estimate n1 n2 / m assumes the lists are independent; when being on one list changes the odds of being on the other by at most a factor kappa, the truth lies within [n1 n2 / (kappa m), kappa n1 n2 / m] (lower, upper), and no data can narrow that box. Chapman's estimate `(n1 + 1)(n2 + 1) / (m + 1)

  • 1` is nearly unbiased, with Seber's standard error.

Usage

crcap(x, kappa = 1, int = NULL)

Arguments

x

c(n1, n2, m), the sizes of two lists and their overlap (named so or in that order), or the seven cells of three lists, named by membership: "100", "010", "001", "110", "101", "011", "111". Counts from 0.

kappa

The largest factor by which being on one list changes the odds of being on the other: one number from 1 (two lists).

int

NULL, or three-way log interactions at which to give the missing cell (three lists).

Value

An object of class crcap, a list: type ("two" or "three"); est, a named vector (two lists: petersen, lower, upper, chapman, se, floor; three: observed, missing, total); pairs (three lists: lists, n1, n2, m, floor, petersen, chapman) and sens (with int: int, missing, total), otherwise NULL.

Details

With three lists the seven observed cells identify the never-listed cell only under an assumption on the three-way interaction of a log-linear model: with none, it is m100 m010 m001 m111 / (m110 m101 m011), and a three-way log interaction t multiplies it by exp(-t); int gives that sensitivity. The pairwise estimates are given beside it, each at least the number seen on either of its two lists (floor). See proof("crcap").

References

Chapman, D. G. (1951). Some properties of the hypergeometric distribution with applications to zoological sample censuses. University of California Publications in Statistics, 1, 131-160.

Seber, G. A. F. (1970). The effects of trap response on tag recapture estimates. Biometrics, 26(1), 13-22.

Fienberg, S. E. (1972). The multiple recapture census for closed populations and incomplete 2^k contingency tables. Biometrika, 59(3), 591-603. doi:10.1093/biomet/59.3.591

Examples

crcap(c(n1 = 500, n2 = 400, m = 80), kappa = 1.5)
#> crcap: two lists 
#>  petersen     lower     upper   chapman        se     floor 
#> 2500.0000 1666.6667 3750.0000 2479.2593  224.0262  820.0000 
crcap(c("100" = 120, "010" = 90, "001" = 60, "110" = 30, "101" = 20,
        "011" = 15, "111" = 8), int = c(-0.5, 0, 0.5))
#> crcap: three lists 
#> observed  missing    total 
#>      343      576      919 
#>  lists  n1  n2  m floor petersen  chapman
#>    1-2 178 143 38   283 669.8421 659.9231
#>    1-3 178 103 28   253 654.7857 640.9310
#>    2-3 143 103 23   223 640.3913 623.0000
#>   int  missing     total
#>  -0.5 949.6635 1292.6635
#>   0.0 576.0000  919.0000
#>   0.5 349.3617  692.3617
